title: The CAIO Mandate
subtitle: From technology leader to enterprise AI executive
summary: Define the CAIO role, its decision rights, its relationship to the CEO/CIO/CTO/CDO/CISO, and the operating outcomes the role is accountable for.

lessons.title: What a CAIO actually owns
lessons.body: Define the CAIO's decisions, peer boundaries, operating cadence, and first-year scorecard. Work through a customer-assistant example and draft your own decision rights.
resources: IBM: What is a Chief AI Officer?
NIST AI Risk Management Framework Core
U.S. OMB M-25-21: federal governance example

lessons.title: Your transition map
lessons.body: Assess what you know and what you can prove. Translate past leadership into CAIO evidence, rank the gaps that matter, and build a 90-day plan with reviewed artifacts.
resources: NIST AI Risk Management Framework Core

lessons.title: Executive stakeholder architecture
lessons.body: Map decision rights across executives, design the forums that move work, resolve a data-and-vendor disagreement, and write an escalation and board-reporting path.
resources: NIST AI Risk Management Framework Core
U.S. OMB M-25-21: federal governance example

quiz.q: Which outcome is most characteristic of a CAIO mandate?
options: Maximizing enterprise value from AI while governing risk
Running only the ML engineering team
Choosing a single foundation model vendor

quiz.q: The most sustainable CAIO operating model is usually:
options: A fully centralized AI team that owns every use case
A governance-only office with no delivery capability
A federated model with central standards and distributed execution

quiz.q: A business team proposes an AI customer assistant. Which division of responsibility is clearest?
options: The CAIO writes every answer and operates support
Product owns the customer workflow; shared teams own standards and controls; the CAIO oversees portfolio and release evidence
The CISO owns the customer journey
The model vendor decides whether to launch

quiz.q: You know how to design an AI governance process but have never led one. What belongs in your transition map?
options: No gap because you know the terminology
An evidence gap with a plan to produce a reviewed governance artifact
A reason to omit governance from your charter

homework: Write a 2-page CAIO charter for a 5,000-person company. Include mission, decision rights, interfaces with CIO/CTO/CDO/CISO, first-year outcomes, and what the CAIO explicitly does not own.

visual.title: From an idea to an accountable decision
